newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jiangxi Copper offers 628 mln H shrs in global IPO.
newsitem.headline: Jiangxi Copper offers 628 mln H shrs in global IPO.

text.p: China copper producer Jiangxi Copper Co Ltd is offering 628.212 million H shares at a maximum HK$2.72 per share in a global offering, the company said in a statement on Monday.
H shares are Hong Kong-listed shares in China-incorporated enterprises.

Ten percent of the issue will be offered to the public in Hong Kong through an initial public offering (IPO) from June 2 to 5, and the balance is earmarked for international placement to institutional investors, the company said.
Dealing in the company's shares is expected to begin on June 12. Merrill Lynch Far East Ltd is the global coordinator of the issue.
Jiangxi Copper is engaged in copper mining, milling, smelting and refining facilities in Jiangxi province in China.
The H shares in the Hong Kong IPO portion would be equally divided into two pools for allocations purposes.

Pool A would be for applications for not more than 1.838 million shares worth about HK$5 million assuming an issue price of HK$2.72, and pool B would be for applications between 1.838 million shares and 31.411 million shares, the statement said.
If one of the pools is undersubscribed, the surplus will be transfered to satisfy demand in the other pool. Applicants can only receive an allocation of shares from either pool A or pool B, it added.

Jiangxi Copper has also granted underwriters an option to require the company to issue an additional 94.23 million shares or 15 percent of the initial share offer, to cover overallotment, the company said in a prospectus.

The company said the indicative price range was from HK$2.13 to HK$2.72, representing a proforma fully-diluted 1997 price earnings ratio of 11 to 14 times. The H shares will have a secondary listing on the London stock Exchange.
From net proceeds of HK$1.3 billion to HK$1.7 billion, about 1.2 billion yuan would be used to repay short-term debt and the balance would go to expand production facilities, it said.

The company's parent, Jiangxi Copper Co, is controlled by the China National Non-Ferrous Metals Corp, which was set up by China's State Council to manage and hold a portion of the non-ferrous metails industry in China.
The company posted a profit of 211.8 million yuan for the ended December 1996, compared with 417 million yuan in 1995 and 192.5 million yuan in 1994.
